bead.title: Fix hybrid-async recovery replay gap at release scale (1M+)
bead.description:
The hybrid-async normal-restart recovery path deterministically fails at 1M+ resident scale with:

    recover hybrid normal restart: Storage("sqlite projection replay gap for tp002:hybrid-recovery: expected sequence 256, got 257")

Reproduced 3/3 runs at PQUEUE_HYBRID_RESIDENT=1000000 (byte-for-byte identical panic each time). Full investigation: .ddx/executions/20260701T224118-e73883ca/hybrid-scale-1m-recovery-gap.md (bead pqueue-d6453cdd).

Root-cause lead (not yet proven with an isolated repro): SegmentedObjectLog::read_manifest sorts manifest entries by manifest `index` (crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:605), and ObjectLog::read_from paginates that index-ordered stream by truncating to `limit` and computing the next resume cursor from the last entry's sequence (crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/compose_log.rs:121-139). If manifest index order and command sequence order can diverge under group-commit sealing (background flusher tick racing the foreground push path), truncating index-ordered entries can silently skip a sequence and/or advance the pagination cursor past a record that was never returned. The compose.rs recovery loop pages with limit=256 (crates/pqueue-engine/src/compose.rs:1102) — matching the exact gap boundary observed.

The bug only manifests once the resident push volume is large enough (1M+) for the background periodic flusher (added by pqueue-8e5e7846, commit 9d15873) to land at least one partial SQLite high-water advance before the push loop completes; at 100k the push finishes too fast for this to happen, so recovery replays from genesis instead and never exercises the buggy tail-resume path.

This blocks pqueue-d6453cdd's AC2 (1M) and AC3 (10M) release evidence gates, both of which require performance_object_log_hybrid_release_10m to pass with bars_met=true at those resident counts.

In scope: root-cause and fix the manifest/sequence ordering or pagination bug in the segmented object log's read_from/read_manifest path (or wherever the actual defect is proven to be); add a regression test that exercises the tail-resume-after-partial-high-water recovery path without needing a full 1M-item run. Out of scope: performance tuning unrelated to this correctness gap.
bead.acceptance:
1. `cargo test -p pqueue-server --test performance_object_log_hybrid_tests performance_object_log_hybrid_tail_replay_after_partial_sqlite_high_water -- --nocapture` passes and covers partial SQLite high-water followed by object-log tail-resume replay.
2. `PQUEUE_LEDGER_DIR=docs/perf/evidence/hybrid-scale PQUEUE_PERF_ENV=1 PQUEUE_HYBRID_RESIDENT=1000000 cargo test -p pqueue-server --release --test performance_object_log_hybrid_tests performance_object_log_hybrid_release_10m -- --ignored --nocapture` passes with bars_met=true.
3. `cargo fmt --check` passes.
